fidelity: F2a — Carbonation Kinetics + Reactor Energy Balance (lumped ODE)
source: Lackner et al. (1995) Energy 20(11):1153-1170; O'Connor et al. (2005) ARC-TR-04-002 NETL aqueous mineral carbonation; Sanna et al. (2014) Chem. Soc. Rev. 43:8049-8080 (mineral carbonation review)

unit.name: Aqueous mineral carbonation batch reactor (Mg-silicate olivine/serpentine, shrinking-core)

reaction.note: Carbonation of forsterite; +2 mol CO2 bound per mol olivine

stoich_CO2_per_mineral.note: 2 Mg sites per forsterite formula unit, 1 CO2 per Mg

A_pre_1_s.note: Arrhenius pre-exponential for surface reaction rate constant (fitted so 185C/115atm/37um gives ~80% in ~1h, O'Connor 2005)

E_act_J_mol.note: Activation energy of carbonation surface reaction, O'Connor (2005) range 50-75 kJ/mol

reaction_order_P.note: First order in CO2 partial pressure / dissolved CO2 driving force

P_ref_atm.note: Reference CO2 partial pressure (NETL aqueous route ~115-150 atm)

dH_rxn_J_molCO2.note: Exothermic enthalpy of carbonation per mol CO2 bound; olivine carbonation ~ -90 kJ/mol CO2 (Lackner 1995)

particle_radius_ref_m.note: Reference particle radius 37 um (-400 mesh, O'Connor 2005 optimum grind)

slurry_mass_kg.note: Total slurry mass (mineral + water, ~15 wt% solids)
